cards.explanation: The answer is that their eyes don't see and their ears don't hear. The LORD says they “…have eyes but do not see…” and “…have ears but do not hear.” (Jeremiah 5:21). The equipment is all there and they still don't see or hear. It's like a phone buzzing in your jacket all afternoon and you never notice.

The answer is the sand. The LORD says He “…set the sand as the boundary for the sea, an enduring barrier it cannot cross?” (Jeremiah 5:22). Think about that for a second, friends. The whole sea held back by something you can pour out of your shoe.

The answer is False. The LORD says “The waves surge, but they cannot prevail. They roar but cannot cross it.” (Jeremiah 5:22). The waves put on a big show and the boundary doesn't budge. The sea stays where He put it every time.

The answer is that they are stubborn and rebellious. The LORD says “…these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts.” (Jeremiah 5:23). Right before it, He talks about the sea and the sand boundary He set for it (Jeremiah 5:22). Then He turns to His people's hearts.

The answer is rains. The LORD “…gives the rains, both autumn and spring, in season…” (Jeremiah 5:24). The same verse says He keeps the appointed weeks of harvest. Rains and harvest weeks, both named in one verse.

The answer is True. The LORD says “Your iniquities have diverted these from you; your sins have deprived you of My bounty.” (Jeremiah 5:25). The gifts were His and the diverting came from their sins. It's heavy to read, friends, and He says it plainly.
The answer is men. The LORD says these wicked men “…set a trap to catch men.” (Jeremiah 5:26). A fowler hides to catch birds, and these ones hide to catch people. That's a hard line to read.

The answer is deceit. The LORD says “Like cages full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit.” (Jeremiah 5:27). A cage full of birds is hard to miss. These houses are just as packed, only with deceit.
The answer is False. The LORD says “Therefore they have become powerful and rich.” (Jeremiah 5:27). Their deceit got them ahead instead of dragging them down. The verse says so plainly, friends.

The answer is the fatherless. The LORD says “They have not taken up the cause of the fatherless, that they might prosper…” (Jeremiah 5:28). These men had plenty and still didn't do it. Next to it He says they haven't defended the rights of the needy.
The answer is that they prophesy falsely. The passage says “The prophets prophesy falsely…” (Jeremiah 5:31). I think that's a heavy line to read, friends.
The answer is their own. The passage says “…the priests rule by their own authority.” (Jeremiah 5:31). The LORD's and the king's aren't named there, friends. Their own is the one the verse gives.

The answer is True. The passage says “My people love it so…” (Jeremiah 5:31). That comes right after the prophets prophesying falsely and the priests ruling by their own authority. That's what makes the closing question hit so hard, bakers.
